summary: This program picks a game level name from a number using the ternary operator, a compact one-line alternative to an if/else chain. With levelNumber set to 17 it prints "intermediate".

lines.code: int levelNumber = 17; // change this value to test
lines.text: The score being classified. Try values below 10 and at or above 20 to see each of the three outcomes.

The ternary operator reads as "condition ? value if true : value if false", and the whole expression produces a value that is assigned to level. If levelNumber is under 10, the result is "novice" and nothing else is evaluated.
When the first test fails, this second ternary runs as the false branch. Reaching here already means levelNumber is 10 or more, so only the upper bound needs checking.
The final false branch is the fallback for anything 20 and above. A ternary must always supply a value for both branches, so this else-equivalent is required.
Prints the single word the chained ternary settled on.
